resources.string: Type — keys go to the focused app
Needs Android 11 or newer. UxSpace activates a shell-uid helper through Wireless Debugging, an Android 11+ feature.
Open Settings → About phone → Software information, then tap “Build number” seven times until it confirms Developer options is unlocked. Return here when done.
Enable Wireless Debugging in Developer options, then return — UxSpace reconnects automatically.

Open Wireless Debugging and tap “Pair device with a pairing code”. With the pair dialog still in front, pull the notification shade down over it and type the 6-digit code into UxSpace\'s pairing notification — that way the dialog never goes to the background, which is what mDNS needs.
Looking for the local ADB service…
Connecting to the local ADB service…
Pairing failed — check the code and that the “Pair device” dialog is still open, then try again.
Lets you enter the wireless-debugging pairing code from the notification shade.
Type the 6-digit code from the Wireless Debugging pair dialog. Pull this shade down over the dialog and answer here — UxSpace pairs while the dialog is still in front.
Connect your VITURE glasses or an external monitor to start.
Glasses connected — tap apps to add screens (up to 3).
Lets UxSpace open the phone keyboard when you tap into a text field on the glasses, so you can type from the phone.
Turn on the UxSpace accessibility service so the phone keyboard opens automatically when you tap a text field in an app on the glasses.
